subject: Draft DPA: Deployment-mode clauses (Dedicated vs Private) and execution
messages:
From: Avery Lutz <avery.lutz@fintech-co.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA comments: handling for Dedicated vs Private deployments

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for sending through the DPA. We've gone through the draft and focused our redlines on three items that are blockers for procurement/regulatory:

1) Subprocessors: we need a stronger commit on pre-notification and a service-level window for objection (we typically ask 30 days, procurement wants 45).
2) Data transfers: for Dedicated deployments where Redwood still manages networking, we require clarity on whether SCCs (or an adequacy mechanism) cover backup/replication to US/third countries.
3) Private/VPC / On-prem: we need explicit language that no Redwood-managed subprocessors will access plaintext customer data (aside from KMS operations) and that HSM/KMS integrations must be customer-controlled keys where possible.

Attached are our redlines (fintech_redlines_080522.pdf). High level asks: 45-day subprocessor notice, an Annex mapping each deployment mode to the specific export/transfer and subprocessor regime, and an explicit callout that Dedicated customers can opt for the stricter Private annex if they purchase Private, with clear pricing and operational steps.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept Annex B (deployment-mode controls) and whether you can provide an updated DPA with DocuSign for signature? We have an internal renewal deadline of 8/25 and would like to close before that.

Thanks,
Avery

--
Avery Lutz
Sr. Counsel, Data & Privacy
FintechCo

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Avery Lutz <avery.lutz@fintech-co.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA comments: handling for Dedicated vs Private deployments

Hi Avery — thanks for the clear redlines and the timeline. Quick summary from our side and proposals to unblock: 

- Subprocessors / notice window: Redwood's standard is 30 days. We can offer 45 days for customers on enterprise contracts (including your renewal), but we need to limit the scope to material subprocessor changes (new compute/storage providers or security-affecting changes). We can add a definition for "material" in Annex A.

- Data transfers for Dedicated: technically Dedicated is reserved capacity running on Redwood-managed hosts. Backups and metrics are stored in region by default; however certain global-control plane functions may route metadata/health telemetry to our US control plane. We will add explicit language in Annex B describing replication, backup locations, and the contractual commitment that customer content will not be exported outside selected regions for backups unless customer agrees. For SCCs: we can include SCCs for transfers from EU to US and list our subprocessors covered by SCCs in Annex C.

- Private / VPC / On-prem: we agree that for Private (VPC) deployments we will support customer-managed encryption keys (bring-your-own-key via KMS/HSM) and can lock down subprocessors so only monitoring and managed-support agents operate (and with limited data access). We cannot promise zero Redwood-employee access in all Private setups (some on-call troubleshooting may require temporary access with customer approval) — we'll add a process for short-lived access, logging, and audit evidence.

Next steps: Rishi (cc) will propose language for Annex B that maps the deployment modes to the controls you asked for. After alignment we'll produce an updated DPA and share via DocuSign.

Best,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

Avery / Soojin — looping in legal drafting notes and a short draft.

On Fri, Aug 14, 2026 at 09:12 AM Avery Lutz <avery.lutz@fintech-co.com> wrote:
> Hi Soojin,
> 
> Thanks for sending through the DPA. We've gone through the draft and focused our redlines on three items that are blockers for procurement/regulatory: ...

Draft highlights I'm proposing for Annex B (deployment-mode controls):
- Table mapping: Hosted (standard DPA + listed subprocessors + SCCs for EU transfers); Dedicated (customer data isolated in reserved capacity; backups remain in-customer-region by default; SCCs apply for cross-border admin functions); Private/VPC/On‑Prem (customer controls keys; Redwood processes limited to support ops; no automatic cross-border replication without customer consent).
- Subprocessor notice: 45 days for material changes for Enterprise customers; 30 days for standard customers. Process: email notice + published subprocessor log + right to object within notice window; if unresolved, fallback to escalation & mitigation plan (not immediate termination).
- Access/forensics: include requirement for audit logs and support for short-term access with prior auth and timeboxed tickets.
- Data egress & backups: explicit commit to keep backups within customer's selected region unless customer signs off.

Attached is an editable draft (DPA_Redwood_20260814_draft.docx) with those sections. If these points look good to you Avery, please confirm and we'll generate a clean version for DocuSign. Also confirm whether the procurement team requires Redwood to agree to a 45-day termination right if the subprocessor objection is not resolved — our preferred approach is a mitigation path and escalation before termination.

Rishi
